claim: Abiraterone improves survival in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
gold_rationale: Documented regulatory and clinical consensus. The pivotal COU-AA-301 phase 3 RCT (de Bono, NEJM 2011, PMID 21612468; NCT00638690) randomized 1195 men with mCRPC progressing after docetaxel to abiraterone+prednisone vs placebo+prednisone and met its PRIMARY endpoint of overall survival: median 14.8 vs 10.9 months, HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.54-0.77, P<0.001). The interim result crossed the pre-specified stopping boundary and the study was unblinded; the pre-crossover final analysis (Fizazi, Lancet Oncol 2012, PMID 22995653) confirmed the OS benefit (15.8 vs 11.2 mo, HR 0.74). On this OS evidence the FDA approved abiraterone (Zytiga) for post-docetaxel mCRPC on 28 Apr 2011 (priority review, NDA 202379), citing the 14.8-vs-10.9-month OS. The benefit is corroborated, not contradicted, in adjacent populations: chemo-naive mCRPC (COU-AA-302 final OS, Ryan, Lancet Oncol 2015, PMID 25601341: 34.7 vs 30.3 mo, HR 0.81, P=0.0033) and metastatic castration-SENSITIVE disease (LATITUDE, Fizazi NEJM 2017, PMID 28578607, HR 0.62; STAMPEDE, James NEJM 2017, PMID 28578639, HR 0.63). The claimed outcome (OS) is a hard clinical endpoint measured directly in the pivotal trial — no surrogate substitution. No RCT contradicts an OS benefit. Consensus verdict: Supported.

baseline.text: Yes. Abiraterone acetate (plus prednisone) improves overall survival in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This was established by the pivotal phase 3 COU-AA-301 trial in post-docetaxel mCRPC, which showed a median OS of 14.8 vs 10.9 months (HR ~0.65) versus placebo/prednisone and led to FDA approval in 2011. The benefit was later confirmed in the chemotherapy-naive setting (COU-AA-302, OS 34.7 vs 30.3 months) and extended to metastatic castration-sensitive disease (LATITUDE and STAMPEDE). Overall survival is a hard endpoint, the effect is consistent and directional across multiple large randomized trials, and no randomized trial contradicts it, so the answer is a confident Yes.

rows.citation: de Bono JS, et al. Abiraterone and increased survival in metastatic prostate cancer. N Engl J Med. 2011;364(21):1995-2005. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1014618 (COU-AA-301, NCT00638690).
rows.integrity_note: Verified via PubMed: MeSH/pub-types = Clinical Trial Phase III + Randomized Controlled Trial + Multicenter; NOT retracted. Pivotal phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled; primary endpoint OS met at pre-specified interim, DSMC unblinded. N=1195, 2:1 (797 abiraterone / 398 placebo) confirmed against NCT00638690 record.
rows.finding: Post-docetaxel mCRPC, N=1195 (2:1). Primary endpoint OS: 14.8 vs 10.9 mo, HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.54-0.77, P<0.001). Exact population and outcome of the claim.

rows.citation: Fizazi K, et al. Abiraterone acetate for mCRPC: final overall survival analysis of the COU-AA-301 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study. Lancet Oncol. 2012;13(10):983-992. DOI:10.1016/S1470-2045(12)70379-0.
rows.integrity_note: Verified via PubMed: Phase III RCT, NOT retracted. Pre-crossover final OS analysis of the pivotal trial (after 775 of prespecified 797 death events). Confirmatory. NOTE: PubMed abstract text erroneously prints 'NCT00091442'; correct registration is NCT00638690/COU-AA-301 — abstract typo only, does not affect data.
rows.finding: Final OS analysis of COU-AA-301 confirms benefit: 15.8 vs 11.2 mo, HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.64-0.86, P<0.0001). Same post-docetaxel mCRPC population, OS endpoint.

rows.citation: Ryan CJ, et al. Abiraterone acetate plus prednisone vs placebo plus prednisone in chemotherapy-naive men with mCRPC (COU-AA-302): final overall survival analysis. Lancet Oncol. 2015;16(2):152-160. DOI:10.1016/S1470-2045(14)71205-7 (NCT00887198).
rows.integrity_note: Verified via PubMed: Phase III RCT, NOT retracted. Confirmatory phase 3 in the adjacent chemo-naive mCRPC population; prespecified final OS analysis (741 of 773 death events). N=1088, 1:1 (546 abiraterone / 542 placebo) confirmed in abstract. Correctly marked population_match=false: this is a SUPPORTING trial in a different population, not a conflicting trial.
rows.finding: Chemotherapy-NAIVE mCRPC, N=1088. Final OS: 34.7 vs 30.3 mo, HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.70-0.93, P=0.0033). Supports OS benefit; population is pre-chemo (claim specifies after chemotherapy).

rows.citation: Ryan CJ, et al. Abiraterone in metastatic prostate cancer without previous chemotherapy. N Engl J Med. 2013;368(2):138-148. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1209096 (COU-AA-302 interim; NCT00887198).
rows.integrity_note: Verified via PubMed: RCT, Multicenter, NOT retracted. Interim analysis; co-primary endpoints rPFS and OS. OS showed favorable trend (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.61-0.93, P=0.01) that did NOT cross the stringent interim efficacy boundary; matured to significance in PMID:25601341. Publication year in PubMed = 2013 (Jan 10 2013 issue); corrected in citation.
rows.finding: Chemo-naive mCRPC interim: radiographic PFS 16.5 vs 8.3 mo (HR 0.53), OS HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.61-0.93) trending in favor, did not cross efficacy boundary. OS is a co-primary endpoint (not a surrogate substitution).

rows.citation: Fizazi K, et al. Abiraterone plus prednisone in metastatic, castration-sensitive prostate cancer (LATITUDE). N Engl J Med. 2017;377(4):352-360. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1704174 (NCT01715285).
rows.integrity_note: Verified via PubMed: Phase III RCT, Multicenter, NOT retracted. Phase 3 in metastatic castration-SENSITIVE (not resistant) disease; co-primary endpoints OS and rPFS. N=1199 randomized. Correctly marked population_match=false (hormone-sensitive vs claim's CRPC), direction=+1 (supporting).
rows.finding: Metastatic castration-SENSITIVE prostate cancer, N=1199. Primary OS: HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.51-0.76, P<0.001). Extends/corroborates OS benefit but in a different (hormone-sensitive) population than the claim.

rows.citation: James ND, et al. Abiraterone for prostate cancer not previously treated with hormone therapy (STAMPEDE). N Engl J Med. 2017;377(4):338-351. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1702900 (NCT00268476).
rows.integrity_note: Verified via PubMed: Phase II/III RCT, Multicenter, NOT retracted. Multi-arm phase 3; abiraterone+ADT vs ADT in hormone-naive (52% metastatic) disease. Primary outcome OS. N=1917 in this comparison. Correctly marked population_match=false (hormone-naive vs post-chemo CRPC), direction=+1 (independent confirmation).
rows.finding: Hormone-naive prostate cancer starting ADT, N=1917 in comparison. OS: HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.76, P<0.001); HR 0.61 in the metastatic subgroup. Independent confirmation of OS benefit; population is hormone-naive, not post-chemo CRPC.

rows.citation: FDA approval of Zytiga (abiraterone acetate) + prednisone for mCRPC after docetaxel, 28 Apr 2011; basis = COU-AA-301 (NCT00638690). FDA press release UCM253055; NDA 202379.
rows.integrity_note: Verified: NCT00638690 confirmed via ClinicalTrials.gov as Phase 3, N=1195, 2:1, primary endpoint Overall Survival, post-docetaxel mCRPC. FDA approval date 28 Apr 2011 and OS basis (14.8 vs 10.9 mo) confirmed via archived FDA press release UCM253055 and J&J/Centocor release; priority review, NDA 202379. Regulatory anchor for the claimed indication.
rows.finding: FDA approved abiraterone for post-docetaxel mCRPC on the OS result of COU-AA-301 (14.8 vs 10.9 mo). Exact claim population and outcome; regulatory consensus = Supported.
